# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrrefrigeratorandtemperaturecontrolledcabinetmodeclusterchangetomodeparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrrefrigeratorandtemperaturecontrolledcabinetmodeclusterchangetomodeparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.


<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# Document: MTRRequestCommandNameForID(_:_:)

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrrequestcommandnameforid(_:_:)
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrrequestcommandnameforid(_:_:)
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Function Availability: iOS 18.2+ · iPadOS 18.2+ · Mac Catalyst 18.2+ · macOS 15.2+ · tvOS 18.2+ · visionOS 2.2+ · watchOS 11.2+

# MTRRequestCommandNameForID(\_:\_:) (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Function  
**Availability:** iOS 18.2+ · iPadOS 18.2+ · Mac Catalyst 18.2+ · macOS 15.2+ · tvOS 18.2+ · visionOS 2.2+ · watchOS 11.2+

Resolve Matter request (client to server) command IDs into a descriptive string.

## Declaration

```swift
func MTRRequestCommandNameForID(_ clusterID: MTRClusterIDType, _ commandID: MTRCommandIDType) -> String!
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

For unknown IDs, a string ‘\<Unknown clusterID %d\>’ (if the cluster ID is not known) or ‘\<Unknown commandID %d\>’ (if the cluster ID is known but the command ID is not known) will be returned.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrrvcoperationalstateclustergohomeparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrrvcoperationalstateclustergohomeparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Objective-C)

## Declaration


<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

## Declaration



<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrserviceareaclusterselectareasparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrserviceareaclusterselectareasparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

**Framework:** Matter

## Declaration


<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# Document: isConcatenated

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrsetuppayload/isconcatenated
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrsetuppayload/isconcatenated
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 26.2+ · iPadOS 26.2+ · Mac Catalyst 26.2+ · macOS 26.2+ · tvOS 26.2+ · visionOS 26.2+ · watchOS 26.2+

# isConcatenated (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 26.2+ · iPadOS 26.2+ · Mac Catalyst 26.2+ · macOS 26.2+ · tvOS 26.2+ · visionOS 26.2+ · watchOS 26.2+

Whether this object represents a concatenated QR Code payload consisting of two or more underlying payloads. If YES, then:

## Declaration

```swift
var isConcatenated: Bool { get }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

- The constituent payloads are exposed in the `subPayloads` property.
- Properties other than `subPayloads` and `qrCodeString` (e.g. `vendorID`, `discriminator`) are not relevant to a concatenated payload and should not be used. If accessed, they will act as if the payload was not in fact concatenated, and return the relevant value associated with the first sub-payload. Mutating such a property will discard the additional sub-payloads.

# concatenated (Objective-C)


<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

- The constituent payloads are exposed in the `subPayloads` property.
- Properties other than `subPayloads` and `qrCodeString` (e.g. `vendorID`, `discriminator`) are not relevant to a concatenated payload and should not be used. If accessed, they will act as if the payload was not in fact concatenated, and return the relevant value associated with the first sub-payload. Mutating such a property will discard the additional sub-payloads.

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrtemperaturecontrolclustersettemperatureparams/serversideprocessingtimeout
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrtemperaturecontrolclustersettemperatureparams/serversideprocessingtimeout
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrtemperaturecontrolclustersettemperatureparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrtemperaturecontrolclustersettemperatureparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Objective-C)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```objectivec
@property (nonatomic, copy, nullable) NSNumber * timedInvokeTimeoutMs;
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrthermostatclusteratomicrequestparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrthermostatclusteratomicrequestparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

## Discussion

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrthermostatclustersetactivepresetrequestparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrthermostatclustersetactivepresetrequestparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrthreadborderroutermanagementclustergetactivedatasetrequestparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrthreadborderroutermanagementclustergetactivedatasetrequestparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: serverSideProcessingTimeout

# serverSideProcessingTimeout (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls how much time, in seconds, we will allow for the server to process the command.

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var serverSideProcessingTimeout: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

If nil, the framework will try to select an appropriate timeout value itself.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrthreadnetworkdirectoryclusteraddnetworkparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrthreadnetworkdirectoryclusteraddnetworkparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

## Declaration


<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

The command will then time out if that much time, plus an allowance for retransmits due to network failures, passes.

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrthreadnetworkdirectoryclustergetoperationaldatasetparams/timedinvoketimeoutms

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.

# Document: timedInvokeTimeoutMs

Source path: documentation/matter/mtrtimesynchronizationclustersettrustedtimesourceparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Canonical documentation: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/matter/mtrtimesynchronizationclustersettrustedtimesourceparams/timedinvoketimeoutms
Description: Framework: Matter Kind: Instance Property Availability: iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

# timedInvokeTimeoutMs (Swift)

**Framework:** Matter  
**Kind:** Instance Property  
**Availability:** iOS 18.4+ · iPadOS 18.4+ · Mac Catalyst 18.4+ · macOS 15.4+ · tvOS 18.4+ · visionOS 2.4+ · watchOS 11.4+

Controls whether the command is a timed command (using Timed Invoke).

## Declaration

```swift
@NSCopying var timedInvokeTimeoutMs: NSNumber? { get set }
```

<a id="discussion"></a>

## Discussion

If nil (the default value), a regular invoke is done for commands that do not require a timed invoke and a timed invoke with some default timed request timeout is done for commands that require a timed invoke.

If not nil, a timed invoke is done, with the provided value used as the timed request timeout.  The value should be chosen small enough to provide the desired security properties but large enough that it will allow a round-trip from the server to the client (for the status response and actual invoke request) within the timeout window.
